title: Biolistic transformation of Emiliania huxleyi
author: Glen Wheeler
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8tzhwp6
materials: Switch the vacuum button to hold.

steps.title: Prepare tungsten beads
steps.instruction: Weigh 60 mg tungsten into a microfuge tube; wash in 1 mL 100 % ethanol, vortex, centrifuge 13 000 rpm for 1 min and discard ethanol; wash four times with 1 mL molecular‑grade water (centrifuge 13 000 rpm for 1 min each, discard water); add 1 mL water, vortex frequently, aliquot 50 µL into microfuge tubes and freeze for later use.

steps.title: Coat beads with plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Thaw a 50 µL tungsten bead aliquot, add 4 µg pUCHsp90 plasmid DNA (Qiagen miniprep) in ≤10 µL volume, add 50 µL 2.5 M CaCl₂ and 20 µL 0.1 M spermidine, vortex gently, incubate 10 min for bead sedimentation, centrifuge 3 s at 2000 rpm and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Ethanol wash of coated beads
steps.instruction: Wash beads with 250 µL 100 % molecular‑grade ethanol, vortex, centrifuge 3 s at 2000 rpm and discard supernatant; add 50 µL 100 % ethanol, vortex frequently while adding 10 µL aliquots to individual macrocarrier discs, and let the discs dry.

steps.title: Store coated macrocarrier discs
steps.instruction: Place the ethanol‑coated macrocarrier discs into a closed Petri dish lined with Whatman filter paper and store at 4 °C until needed.

steps.title: Grow E. huxleyi culture
steps.instruction: Grow Emiliania huxleyi (CCMP1516) for 4–7 days to reach a cell density of 5 × 10⁵ – 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Clean biolistic device
steps.instruction: Wipe the outside and inside of the PDS‑1000/He chamber with ethanol; briefly immerse rupture discs, macrocarrier holders and stopping screens in ethanol and let dry.

steps.title: Connect gas and vacuum
steps.instruction: Connect the PDS‑1000 apparatus to a helium supply and to a vacuum pump.

steps.title: Assemble biolistic apparatus
steps.instruction: Set up the apparatus according to the manufacturer’s instructions; place the stopping screen on the shelf, insert the macrocarrier disc (beads facing down) into the holder, position over the screen, screw the assembly together, and place the launch assembly onto the uppermost shelf of the chamber.

steps.title: Prepare cell filter
steps.instruction: Filter 150 mL E. huxleyi culture onto a 47 mm diameter 3 µm cellulose nitrate membrane (Whatman); wash the filter with 3–5 mL biolistic loading buffer to remove excess salt, keep the filter damp, and transfer it to a 47 mm Petri dish.

steps.title: Position filter for bombardment
steps.instruction: Place the Petri dish containing the damp filter onto the target plate shelf in the biolistic chamber, 6 cm below the macrocarrier launch assembly.

steps.title: Install rupture disc
steps.instruction: Remove the rupture‑disc retaining cap, insert a new rupture disc, and re‑install the cap.

steps.title: Load and fire particles
steps.instruction: Turn on the vacuum pump, set the vacuum button to VAC and evacuate the chamber until the pressure reaches 27 in Hg; release the FIRE button and set the vacuum button to VENT; press and hold FIRE until the rupture disc bursts and the DNA‑tungsten beads are propelled onto the cells.

steps.title: Recover transformed cells
steps.instruction: Remove the Petri dish, replace its lid (beads should be visible on the filter centre), wash cells off the filter with 3 mL 50 % salinity F/2 medium into a sterile culture dish, and incubate overnight (~16 h) in a light‑chamber incubator.

steps.title: Select and count transformants
steps.instruction: Count cells with a haemocytometer to assess survival (should approximate the starting density); dispense 10 µL of cells into each well of a 24‑well plate and bring the volume to 2 mL with 50 % salinity F/2 medium containing 80 µg mL⁻¹ nourseothricin; include control wells of non‑transformed cells with and without nourseothricin; observe wells weekly for cell health (motility, integrity) and perform cell counts.
